visualBrief: Complete connected principal Dolmabahçe Palace exterior: two-story pale selamlik/main-entry group, much taller ceremonial hall and flanking links, long harem waterfront and full inland return. Real recessed closed windows/doors, paired pilasters, layered cornices, original simplified pediments, parapets, gray hipped roofs and glazed roof lanterns. Principal native plan and front rounded stair are retained; two submeter seam strips close native digitization gaps between the three attached groups. Detached pavilion/museum, clock tower, mosque, garden gates, seawall, red-roofed services, gardens and city remain independent. No copied heraldry, text, statues or interiors.

references.observed: Actually inspected broad aerial from the sea: continuous pale principal palace with three major waterfront groups, a much taller square ceremonial-hall block and low gray hipped/terraced roofs. The long harem group has repeated projecting bays and a rear wing extending inland. A detached pale waterfront pavilion lies beyond a visible garden gap and is not automatically part of the principal model. Rear red-roofed service buildings and gardens remain independent until ownership is established.

Actually inspected close frontal ceremonial-hall facade: raised square pale-stone central hall, tall upper arched glazing between pilasters, lower arched windows, strong cornice/pediment relief and broad low gray hipped roof. Lower connected wings flank it. A separate ornate waterfront gate aligns with the hall; no heraldry or lettering is copied. Photo perspective plus mapped plan can set original relative height, not a surveyed height.

Actually inspected oblique southwest/main-entry end: full two-story pale palace group, recessed upper/lower fenestration, projecting corners and central roof lantern/skylight. Connected lower roofs lead toward the tall ceremonial hall and northern ranges. Gray pitched roofs contrast with the pale stone facade; ornate detached garden gate, waterfront balustrade and trees provide context. Do not copy the broadcast overlay or inscriptions.
